order.note: Basic backpack first and it is genuinely cheap - chest, leather, string. Guides open here and never treat it as a milestone, just the entry ticket.
The upgrade base is the second thing you make and the one most players under-rate. Iron + leather + string, and almost every upgrade in the mod is built on top of one.

Only then tier the backpack up. The guide's framing is that tiers buy UPGRADE SLOTS, not just rows - the basic bag has a single upgrade slot, netherite has many - so upgrades and tiers are climbed together.
First upgrades reached for are the ones that change moment-to-moment play: pickup, then magnet, then filter.

ladder.note: Backpack tier ladder. Copper is an OPTIONAL side step, not a required rung - the jar carries both backpack->iron and copper->iron recipes, matching the guide's 'there's also a copper variant, if you'd rather'. Netherite is the one break in the pattern: it is a smithing-table recipe, not a crafting one.

Stack-multiplier ladder, each rung a metal STORAGE BLOCK: copper block, iron block, gold block, diamond block, netherite block. The guide quotes 1.5x/2x/4x/8x/16x and flags tier 4 as 'blocks of netherite, which is obviously crazy'. An omega tier exists above tier 4 that the guide never mentions.
Every functional upgrade has a basic and an 'advanced' rung, and the advanced one is crafted FROM the basic (redstone + gold + diamond). So the upgrade tree is two-deep everywhere, not flat.

Hidden rung the guide glosses over: the magnet upgrade is not built from an upgrade base at all, it is built FROM the pickup upgrade. Pickup is a hard prerequisite for magnet, and advanced pickup for advanced magnet.
Cooking upgrades chain sideways rather than up: smelting converts into smoking or blasting, and each auto- variant is the next tier of its base with a hopper.

gates.note: The upgrade base gates nearly the whole mod - every upgrade except the backpack tiers and the pickup-derived magnet needs one in its recipe. This is the mod's true tech gate.

Upgrade SLOTS gate how many upgrades can actually be worn at once, so a low-tier backpack caps the build regardless of which upgrades are crafted. The guide demonstrates this by switching to a netherite bag to show the upgrades at all.
Netherite backpack needs a smithing table, a smithing template and a netherite ingot - it cannot be crafted on a bench like the other tiers.
The chipped/* workstation upgrades each need the matching Chipped mod block, so they are gated behind another mod entirely. Chipped IS present in this pack, so these are legitimately reachable here.

payoff.note: The pickup/magnet pair is where the mod clicks for most players - loot walks into the bag and mining stops being an inventory-management game.
The everlasting upgrade is called out as 'very useful' - indestructible, cannot despawn, cannot fall into the void. It removes the one real fear of carrying everything in one bag.
Inception - backpacks inside backpacks - is described as a 'crazy amount of storage'. A natural late milestone.
The crafting and auto-smelting upgrades turn the bag into a portable workshop, which is the other 'why would I ever put this down' moment.
Feeding upgrade is praised for its precision - it can be told to only eat when no hunger would be wasted, and to skip foods whose buffs you are saving.

traps.note: The infinity upgrade has NO recipe in the jar - it is an admin/creative item. The guide notices this live ('there's no recipe for it in the pack I'm playing'). Never make it a quest reward or task.
Tool swapper is the one upgrade the guide openly dismisses: 'I don't see a massive use for that one.'

Stack downgrades read like a mistake but are deliberate - they DIVIDE a slot's capacity, and exist only to make filtered slots hold less. Not a progression item; do not place them on an upgrade ladder.
Everlasting and inception are gated behind nether stars (and an end crystal), so despite sounding like quality-of-life they are post-Wither items, not mid-game ones.

signature.note: The bag itself and the universal upgrade component - the two items the whole mod hangs off.
The upgrades that define the mod's identity versus every other backpack mod: it is a programmable container, not a bigger bag.
